title: Business and Work
objectives: Làm dạng matching features: nối ý kiến/phát hiện với đúng người
Phân biệt fact, opinion và theory trong bài đọc học thuật
Viết Task 2 dạng advantages/disadvantages với hai mặt cân bằng
Dùng will/going to và từ nối nhượng bộ (although, despite, however) chính xác
exam_strategy: Matching features: gạch dưới tên người trong bài trước, rồi đọc kỹ những gì mỗi người nói; câu hỏi là paraphrase của ý kiến, không lặp lại nguyên văn.
core_outcome: Tách luận điểm của từng người; viết Task 2 hai mặt cân bằng mà vẫn trả lời đúng câu hỏi của đề.
vocabulary: A second language can improve your career prospects.
sự hài lòng với công việc
Job satisfaction depends on more than salary.

Many start-ups fail within their first three years.
Flexible hours help parents balance work and family.
The company pays for professional development courses.

tỉ lệ nghỉ việc của nhân viên

sức khỏe và sự an vui của nhân viên

grammar.title: Future forms (will / going to) and concessive linking
grammar.explanation_vi: will dùng cho dự đoán chung và quyết định ngay lúc nói; be going to dùng cho kế hoạch đã định hoặc dự đoán có bằng chứng hiện tại. Để nối hai ý trái ngược: although/even though + mệnh đề; despite/in spite of + danh từ hoặc V-ing; however đứng đầu câu thứ hai, sau dấu chấm và có dấu phẩy.
grammar.form: will + V (dự đoán, quyết định tức thời) · be going to + V (kế hoạch, dự đoán có căn cứ) · Although + S + V, … · Despite + N/V-ing, … · … . However, …
examples: Automation will probably change many office jobs in the next decade.
The company is going to open two new branches next year.
Although remote working saves time, some employees feel isolated.
examples_vi: Tự động hóa có lẽ sẽ thay đổi nhiều công việc văn phòng trong thập kỷ tới.
Công ty dự định mở thêm hai chi nhánh vào năm sau.
Mặc dù làm việc từ xa tiết kiệm thời gian, một số nhân viên cảm thấy cô lập.
grammar.trap: Despite KHÔNG đi với mệnh đề: viết “Despite the high salary” hoặc “Although the salary is high”, không viết “Despite the salary is high”. Không dùng although và but trong cùng một câu.
items: Look at those dark clouds – it ___ (rain). (be going to)
is going to rain
Dự đoán có bằng chứng ngay trước mắt → be going to.
I think robots ___ (replace) some factory jobs in the future.
will replace
Dự đoán chung dựa trên ý kiến (I think) → will.
We have already booked the venue. We ___ (hold) the conference in May.
are going to hold
Kế hoạch đã sắp xếp → be going to.
___ the long hours, she enjoys her job. (Despite / Although)
Despite
Sau chỗ trống là cụm danh từ (the long hours) → Despite.
___ the pay is low, the job offers good training. (Despite / Although)
Although
Sau chỗ trống là mệnh đề (the pay is low) → Although.
The office is modern. ___, it is far from the city centre. (từ nối đầu câu)
However
However đứng đầu câu thứ hai, theo sau là dấu phẩy.
The phone is ringing. Don’t worry – I ___ (answer) it.
will answer
Quyết định ngay lúc nói → will.
Correct the error: Although the salary was good, but he left the company.
Although the salary was good, he left the company.
Không dùng although và but cùng lúc.

readings.title: Is the four-day week the future of work?
readings.strategy: Matching features: tìm và gạch dưới mọi tên người (Okoro, Lindqvist, Ramos…) trong bài; với mỗi câu hỏi, đọc lại phần ý kiến của từng người. Một người có thể là đáp án cho nhiều câu.
readings.instruction_vi: Bài đọc khoảng 700 từ, 11 câu: 6 câu nối ý kiến với người nói (matching features) và 5 câu FACT / OPINION / THEORY... được gộp thành short-answer và multiple choice.
paragraphs: A

For most of the past century, the five-day working week has been treated as normal in many countries. Recently, however, a growing number of companies have experimented with a four-day week in which employees work around thirty-two hours instead of forty, without any reduction in pay. Supporters claim that this arrangement makes staff healthier and more productive. Critics argue that it is only possible in certain industries and could damage businesses that depend on serving customers every day.
B

One of the largest trials took place across sixty organisations in the fictional country of Norland, involving around three thousand employees. The organisations ranged from software developers and accountants to a restaurant chain and a small manufacturing firm. Each agreed to try a four-day week for six months while researchers measured productivity, staff wellbeing and customer satisfaction. At the end of the trial, fifty-one of the sixty organisations decided to continue with the shorter week.
C

Dr Grace Okoro, an economist who led the research team, believes the most important finding was that productivity did not fall in most organisations. “When people know they have less time, they cut out the activities that add little value – unnecessary meetings, long email chains, tasks done twice,” she explains. In her view, many offices had been measuring effort by the number of hours staff were seen at their desks, rather than by what they actually produced.
D

Staff wellbeing improved even more clearly. Employees reported sleeping better, exercising more often and spending more time with their families. The number of sick days fell by around a third. Psychologist Erik Lindqvist, who analysed the questionnaires, points out that the extra day off was not simply used for rest. “Many people used it for the tasks that normally fill up their weekend – shopping, appointments, cleaning – so that the weekend itself became genuinely free.”
E

Not every organisation found the change easy. The restaurant chain struggled because customers expected it to be open seven days a week, and it had to hire additional part-time staff to cover the gaps. Its operations manager, Luis Ramos, says the trial was worthwhile but expensive. “For an office, a four-day week can mean everyone is off on Friday. For us, it means complicated timetables and higher wage costs. It works, but not for free.”
F

Some researchers question whether the results will last. Professor Hana Sato, who studies working practices but was not involved in the trial, suggests that companies which volunteer for such experiments are likely to be well organised and enthusiastic from the start. She also argues that the excitement of trying something new may have encouraged people to work harder during the trial. “We need to know what happens after three or four years, when the four-day week is no longer new,” she says.
G

There are also questions about who benefits. In the Norland trial, office workers found it much easier to reduce their hours than staff in shops, hospitals or transport, where a fixed number of people must be present at all times. Dr Okoro accepts this limitation but argues that such sectors could still explore shorter or more flexible schedules. Lindqvist adds that a society in which only some workers enjoy a four-day week could become more unequal.
H

For now, the four-day week is likely to spread gradually rather than suddenly. Several governments are considering further trials, and some companies now advertise a shorter week as a way to attract skilled staff. Whether it eventually becomes as normal as the five-day week did a century ago may depend less on the evidence from trials than on whether employers and workers can agree on how its costs and benefits should be shared.

questions.prompt: Who says that some workplaces judged employees by time spent at their desks?
questions.why: Đoạn C: Okoro nói nhiều văn phòng đo nỗ lực bằng số giờ nhân viên ngồi ở bàn.

questions.prompt: Who explains how employees used their extra day?
questions.why: Đoạn D: Lindqvist nói ngày nghỉ thêm dùng cho mua sắm, hẹn khám, dọn dẹp.

questions.prompt: Who says the shorter week increased costs for their business?
questions.why: Đoạn E: Ramos nói lịch phức tạp và chi phí lương cao hơn – “not for free”.

questions.prompt: Who suggests that the organisations in the trial may not be typical?
questions.why: Đoạn F: các công ty tự nguyện thử nghiệm thường đã tổ chức tốt và hào hứng từ đầu.

questions.prompt: Who warns that the four-day week could increase inequality?
questions.why: Đoạn G: Lindqvist nói xã hội chỉ một số người được làm 4 ngày có thể bất bình đẳng hơn.

questions.prompt: Who believes long-term evidence is still needed?
questions.why: Đoạn F: “We need to know what happens after three or four years”.

questions.prompt: How many organisations took part in the Norland trial? Write ONE NUMBER.
questions.why: Đoạn B: “sixty organisations”.

questions.prompt: How many organisations chose to keep the four-day week? Write ONE NUMBER.
questions.why: Đoạn B: “fifty-one of the sixty organisations decided to continue”.

questions.prompt: By how much did sick days fall? Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.why: Đoạn D: “fell by around a third” – chấp nhận a third.

questions.prompt: Which statement from the passage is a THEORY rather than a measured fact?
options: A. Around three thousand employees took part.
B. Sick days fell by around a third.
C. The excitement of something new may have made people work harder.
D. The trial lasted six months.
questions.answer: C. The excitement of something new may have made people work harder.
questions.why: Đoạn F: Sato đưa ra giả thuyết (“may have encouraged”), chưa được đo lường. A, B, D là số liệu kiểm chứng được.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest in paragraph H?
options: A. The four-day week will become normal very soon.
B. Its future depends on how costs and benefits are shared.
C. Governments have stopped all trials.
D. Only skilled staff want a shorter week.
questions.answer: B. Its future depends on how costs and benefits are shared.
questions.why: Đoạn H: phụ thuộc vào việc chủ và người lao động thống nhất chia sẻ chi phí–lợi ích.

readings.title: Why small cafés close – and why some survive
readings.strategy: Sentence endings: đọc phần đầu câu, tìm đoạn liên quan, rồi chọn phần kết khớp cả ngữ pháp lẫn ý nghĩa; loại phần kết đúng ngữ pháp nhưng sai ý.
paragraphs: A

Opening a café is one of the most popular choices for first-time business owners, and also one of the riskiest. In the fictional city of Larkford, records show that nearly half of new cafés close within three years. Researchers at the local business school interviewed the owners of forty cafés – some that had failed and some that were still trading – to understand what made the difference.
B

Rent was the most frequently mentioned problem. Owners who chose busy shopping streets often paid three or four times more than those in quieter residential areas, and many underestimated how many cups of coffee they would need to sell each day simply to cover their costs. Several successful owners said they had deliberately chosen cheaper locations near offices or schools, where they could build a regular group of customers.
C

Market research also mattered. Owners who failed were more likely to have opened the kind of café they personally liked, without checking whether local people wanted it. One owner opened an expensive specialist coffee shop in an area where most residents were retired and preferred tea and cake at lower prices. By contrast, survivors had usually spent weeks observing the area, counting passers-by and talking to potential customers before signing a lease.
D

Staff turnover was a hidden cost. Cafés that paid only the minimum wage and offered no training found that employees left within a few months, which meant constant recruitment and inconsistent service. Owners of long-lasting cafés often described their staff as the main reason customers returned, and several paid above the minimum wage despite their small profit margins.
E

Finally, the survivors were more willing to change. Many had added services after opening – breakfast menus for office workers, evening events, delivery or space for small meetings – once they had learned what their customers needed. The researchers concluded that a café’s success depends less on its first idea than on how quickly the owner can learn and adapt. As one long-standing owner put it, the menu on the wall today looks almost nothing like the one she started with.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: Owners in busy shopping streets often…
options: B. paid much higher rent than others.
C. built a group of regular customers quickly.
questions.answer: B. paid much higher rent than others.
questions.why: Đoạn B: “paid three or four times more”.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: Many owners who failed…
options: A. opened a café based on their own taste.
B. counted passers-by for several weeks.
C. paid staff above the minimum wage.
questions.answer: A. opened a café based on their own taste.
questions.why: Đoạn C: “opened the kind of café they personally liked, without checking”.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: Cafés that offered no training…
options: A. had the best customer service.
B. lost staff within a few months.
questions.answer: B. lost staff within a few months.
questions.why: Đoạn D: “employees left within a few months”.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: According to the researchers, a café’s success depends mainly on…
options: C. how quickly the owner adapts.
D. the size of the building.
questions.answer: C. how quickly the owner adapts.
questions.why: Đoạn E: “depends less on its first idea than on how quickly the owner can learn and adapt”.

questions.prompt: What proportion of new cafés in Larkford close within three years? Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.why: Đoạn A: “nearly half of new cafés close within three years”.

questions.prompt: How many café owners were interviewed? Write ONE NUMBER.
questions.why: Đoạn A: “the owners of forty cafés”.

questions.prompt: What did most residents in one area prefer, apart from cake? Write ONE WORD.
questions.why: Đoạn C: “preferred tea and cake at lower prices”.

questions.prompt: Name ONE service survivors added for office workers. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
questions.why: Đoạn E: “breakfast menus for office workers”.

readings.title: Learning on the job: apprenticeships return
readings.strategy: Fact – opinion – theory: fact có số liệu/sự kiện; opinion có từ đánh giá (should, best, I believe); theory là giải thích chưa được chứng minh (may, could, suggests).
paragraphs: A

For many years, young people in the fictional country of Carvia were told that a university degree was the safest route to a good career. Apprenticeships – in which trainees work for an employer while studying part-time – were often seen as a second choice for those who did not do well at school. That view is now changing. Over the past five years, the number of apprenticeships in Carvia has risen by forty per cent, and they now cover areas such as software engineering, accounting and healthcare as well as traditional trades.
B

One obvious attraction is cost. Apprentices are paid a salary from the first day, and their training fees are covered by the employer and the government, so most finish without any debt. University graduates in Carvia, by contrast, leave with an average debt equal to about two years’ starting salary.
C

Employers also report benefits. A survey of three hundred companies found that apprentices were more likely than graduate recruits to stay with the company for at least five years. Some managers believe this is because apprentices feel loyal to an employer that invested in them; others suggest that they simply have a clearer idea of the job before they commit to it.
D

Not everyone is convinced. Some teachers argue that apprenticeships force young people to choose a career too early, at sixteen or eighteen, when many do not yet know what they want to do. A degree, they say, keeps more options open. In the view of the national students’ association, the best system would make it easier to move between the two routes, so that an apprentice could later go to university and a graduate could retrain through an apprenticeship.
E

Whatever the debate, demand is rising. In the most popular programmes, there are now more than ten applicants for every place, which suggests that apprenticeships are no longer seen as an easy option. Several employers have started visiting secondary schools to explain what apprentices actually do, hoping to reach students before they make their final choice about university.

questions.prompt: Statement: The number of apprenticeships in Carvia has risen by forty per cent.
questions.why: Đoạn A: số liệu kiểm chứng được.

questions.prompt: Statement: Apprentices stay longer because they feel loyal to an employer that invested in them.
questions.why: Đoạn C: “Some managers believe this is because…” – giải thích chưa được chứng minh.

questions.prompt: Statement: The best system would make it easier to move between the two routes.
questions.why: Đoạn D: “In the view of … the best system would…” – quan điểm.

questions.prompt: Statement: In the most popular programmes, there are more than ten applicants per place.
questions.why: Đoạn E: số liệu.

questions.prompt: Apprentices in Carvia pay their own training fees.
questions.why: Đoạn B: phí đào tạo do chủ doanh nghiệp và chính phủ chi trả.

questions.prompt: Some teachers think sixteen is too young to choose a career.
questions.why: Đoạn D: “force young people to choose a career too early, at sixteen or eighteen”.

questions.prompt: Graduates’ average debt is equal to about how much starting salary? Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.why: Đoạn B: “about two years’ starting salary” – chấp nhận two years.

questions.prompt: How many companies took part in the employer survey? Write ONE NUMBER.
questions.why: Đoạn C: “three hundred companies”.

questions.prompt: Where have some employers started visiting to explain apprenticeships? Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.
questions.why: Đoạn E: “visiting secondary schools”.

listenings.title: Students discuss their work placements
listenings.strategy: Matching thái độ: nghe cách người nói đánh giá (“the best part”, “I was disappointed”), không chỉ chủ đề họ nhắc tới. Có thể có người đổi ý giữa chừng.
listenings.pre_listening: Trước khi nghe: đọc danh sách ý kiến A–F và đoán từ đồng nghĩa.
listenings.trap: Người nói có thể bắt đầu bằng một nhận xét rồi đổi ý (“at first I thought…, but…”); đáp án là ý kiến cuối cùng.
listenings.transcript:
Tutor: Right, I’d like each of you to tell me briefly how your work placement went. Priya, you were at the marketing agency.
Priya: Yes. At first I was worried I’d just be making coffee, but they gave me real responsibility almost immediately. By the second week I was running social media for a small client. The best part was definitely being trusted with real work.
Tutor: Good. Ben, you were at the bank?
Ben: That’s right. To be honest, I found it quite repetitive. Most days I was checking spreadsheets. But I did learn a lot from my supervisor – she explained how every decision was made. So the people were the most valuable part for me, more than the tasks.
Tutor: Interesting. Chloe?
Chloe: I was at an engineering firm. I enjoyed the technical work, but I was surprised by how much time everyone spent in meetings. I think I learned more about communication than about engineering, which wasn’t what I expected.
Tutor: And Daniel, the hotel?
Daniel: My placement made me change my plans completely. I always thought I wanted to work in hotel management, but after six weeks of night shifts I realised it isn’t for me. I’m now thinking about a career in event planning instead.
Tutor: That’s still a useful result. Emma?
Emma: I was at a small start-up. It was exciting, but very disorganised – nobody had time to train me. Still, I’d say the most important thing I gained was confidence, because I had to solve problems on my own.
Tutor: Thank you all. For your reports, remember to include at least one thing you would do differently next time.

questions.prompt: Priya – what did she value most?
options: A. Being trusted with real work
E. Discovering a different career path
questions.answer: A. Being trusted with real work
questions.why: “The best part was definitely being trusted with real work.”

questions.prompt: Ben – what did he value most?
options: A. Being trusted with real work
E. Discovering a different career path
questions.why: Công việc lặp lại, nhưng “the people were the most valuable part”.

questions.prompt: Chloe – what did she mainly learn about?
options: A. Being trusted with real work
E. Discovering a different career path
questions.why: “I learned more about communication than about engineering”.

questions.prompt: Daniel – what was the result of his placement?
options: A. Being trusted with real work
E. Discovering a different career path
questions.answer: E. Discovering a different career path
questions.why: Daniel nhận ra quản lý khách sạn không hợp, chuyển hướng sang event planning.

questions.prompt: Emma – what did she gain most?
options: A. Being trusted with real work
E. Discovering a different career path
questions.why: “the most important thing I gained was confidence”.

questions.prompt: What did Ben dislike about his placement?
questions.why: “I found it quite repetitive … checking spreadsheets” – chấp nhận it was repetitive.

questions.prompt: What surprised Chloe at the engineering firm? Time spent in ______
questions.why: “how much time everyone spent in meetings”.

questions.prompt: What must students include in their reports? One thing they would do ______ next time.
questions.why: “include at least one thing you would do differently next time”.

listenings.title: Enquiring about a part-time job
listenings.strategy: Nghe giờ làm, mức lương theo giờ và yêu cầu công việc; chú ý con số được sửa.
listenings.transcript:
Manager: Greenway Garden Centre, Sophie speaking.
Caller: Hello, I’m calling about the part-time job you advertised – the weekend sales assistant.
Manager: Ah yes. Are you a student?
Caller: I am, I’m in my second year at university, studying biology.
Manager: That could be useful – we get lots of questions about plants. The job is on Saturdays and Sundays. On Saturdays you’d work from eight until four, and on Sundays from ten until four.
Caller: That’s fine. What’s the pay?
Manager: It’s eleven pounds fifty an hour. The advert said eleven, but that was before the minimum wage went up.
Caller: Great. What would I be doing?
Manager: Mainly helping customers and working on the till. In spring we also need people to water the plants in the outdoor area first thing in the morning.
Caller: Do I need any experience?
Manager: Not really, but you must be able to lift heavy bags of compost, up to twenty kilos. And you’ll need to wear safety boots, which we provide.
Caller: OK. Is there any training?
Manager: Yes, there’s a half-day induction on your first Saturday, covering health and safety and how to use the till.
Caller: How do I apply?
Manager: Send a short CV and covering letter by email to jobs at greenway dot co dot uk. The closing date is the thirtieth of April, and interviews will be held the following week.
Caller: Thank you very much.
Manager: Good luck – and mention that you spoke to Sophie.

questions.prompt: Job title: weekend ______ assistant
questions.why: “the weekend sales assistant”.

questions.prompt: Caller’s subject at university: ______
questions.why: “studying biology”.

questions.prompt: Saturday hours: 8 a.m. until ______
questions.why: “from eight until four” – chấp nhận 4 p.m.

questions.prompt: Pay per hour: £______
questions.why: £11 là số cũ trong quảng cáo (bẫy); nay £11.50.

questions.prompt: Spring task: watering plants in the ______ area
questions.why: “water the plants in the outdoor area”.

questions.prompt: Maximum weight to lift: ______ kg
questions.why: “up to twenty kilos”.

questions.prompt: Provided by employer: safety ______
questions.why: “safety boots, which we provide”.

questions.prompt: Closing date: 30th ______
questions.why: “the thirtieth of April”.

listenings.title: Lecture: why people stay in their jobs
listenings.strategy: Bài giảng liệt kê các yếu tố; ghi chú theo số thứ tự (first, second…) và chú ý ví dụ minh họa cho từng yếu tố.
listenings.transcript:
Lecturer: Last week we looked at why people leave their jobs. Today I want to turn that question around and ask why people stay. Staff turnover is expensive – replacing an employee can cost up to half of their annual salary – so understanding what keeps people is valuable for any organisation.
The first factor, perhaps surprisingly, is not pay. Salary matters when people choose a job, but once they are paid fairly, small increases have little effect on whether they stay. In one large survey, only fifteen per cent of employees named salary as the main reason they remained with their employer.
The factor mentioned most often was the relationship with their direct manager. People who felt their manager listened to them and recognised their work were far more likely to stay, even when other companies offered more money.
The second factor is growth. Employees want to feel that they are learning and moving forward. Companies that offer professional development, such as training courses or the chance to work on new projects, tend to keep staff longer. Interestingly, the opportunity to learn seems to matter more to younger workers than a promotion.
Third, flexibility. Since many people began working from home, flexible hours have become one of the most valued benefits. For parents in particular, the ability to start and finish at different times can be more important than a higher salary.
Finally, meaning. People are more likely to stay when they understand how their work contributes to something they care about. A hospital cleaner who understands that clean wards prevent infections, for example, often describes the job very differently from one who has never been told this.
For next week, please read the case study on the logistics company and identify which of these four factors it improved.

questions.prompt: Cost of replacing an employee: up to ______ of annual salary
questions.why: “up to half of their annual salary”.

questions.prompt: Employees who named salary as the main reason for staying: ______
questions.why: “only fifteen per cent”.

questions.prompt: Factor mentioned most often: relationship with the direct ______
questions.why: “the relationship with their direct manager”.

questions.prompt: For younger workers, the chance to ______ matters more than promotion.
questions.why: “the opportunity to learn seems to matter more to younger workers than a promotion”.

questions.prompt: Group for whom flexible hours are especially important: ______
questions.why: “For parents in particular”.

questions.prompt: Fourth factor: ______
questions.why: “Finally, meaning.”

questions.prompt: Example: a hospital cleaner understands that clean wards prevent ______
questions.why: “clean wards prevent infections”.

questions.prompt: Next week’s reading: a case study on a ______ company
questions.why: “the case study on the logistics company”.

writing.instruction_vi: Đề hỏi lợi và hại: mỗi thân bài một mặt, có giải thích và ví dụ; nếu đề hỏi “Do the advantages outweigh…?” thì phải nêu rõ kết luận bên nào nặng hơn. Viết ít nhất 250 từ trong 40 phút.
writing.task: More and more people are working from home rather than travelling to an office. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend? Write at least 250 words.
writing.sample_answer:
In recent years, a growing number of employees have started to work from home for at least part of the week instead of commuting to an office. This trend has clear benefits for both workers and employers, but it also creates some significant problems.

The most obvious advantage of working from home is the time and money saved on commuting. Someone who spends an hour travelling each way gains ten hours a week, which can be used for rest, exercise or family. Remote work also allows companies to reduce the cost of office space and to recruit talented staff who live far from the city. In addition, many employees find that they can concentrate better at home, away from the noise and interruptions of an open-plan office, which may increase their productivity.

On the other hand, working from home has several drawbacks. Many people feel isolated when they rarely see colleagues, and this can affect both their wellbeing and their sense of belonging to the company. Young employees may suffer most, because they learn a great deal by watching and asking experienced colleagues, which is harder to do online. Furthermore, when the home becomes the workplace, it can be difficult to separate work from private life, and some people end up working longer hours rather than shorter ones.

In conclusion, working from home offers valuable savings in time and cost and can improve concentration, but it may also lead to loneliness, slower learning for new staff and longer working hours. A combination of home and office work may therefore be the most effective arrangement for many organisations.
guidance: Mở bài: paraphrase xu hướng + câu định hướng (bài sẽ bàn cả lợi và hại).
Thân bài 1: 2–3 lợi ích, mỗi ý có giải thích/ví dụ.
Thân bài 2: 2–3 bất lợi, dùng On the other hand / Furthermore.
Kết luận: tóm tắt hai mặt; có thể đề xuất giải pháp kết hợp.

essay.prompt: Some people think it is better for young people to start their own business, while others believe they should first gain experience working for a company. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
planning_prompts: Mở bài: nêu hai quan điểm và ý kiến của bạn.
Thân bài 1: lợi ích của khởi nghiệp sớm (sáng tạo, ít trách nhiệm gia đình, học từ thất bại).
Thân bài 2: lợi ích của làm cho công ty trước (kinh nghiệm, mạng lưới, vốn).
Kết luận: quan điểm rõ ràng, có điều kiện.
model_paragraphs: Starting a business is an attractive idea for many young people, and opinions differ on whether they should do so immediately or after working for an established company. While there are good arguments on both sides, I believe that most young people benefit from gaining some experience first.

Those who support starting a business early argue that youth is the best time to take risks. Young people usually have fewer financial responsibilities, such as mortgages or children, so failure is less damaging. They may also have fresh ideas and be more comfortable with new technology than older competitors. Even if their first business fails, the lessons they learn can help them succeed later.

On the other hand, working for a company first offers valuable preparation. Employees can observe how a successful organisation manages customers, finances and staff without risking their own money. They also build a network of contacts, including potential clients, suppliers and future partners. In addition, a few years of salary allows them to save money, which reduces the need for large loans when they eventually start their own business.

In my view, the second approach is more sensible for most people. Many new businesses fail not because the idea is poor, but because the owner lacks practical skills such as budgeting or hiring. Two or three years in a company can provide exactly these skills.

In conclusion, starting a business at a young age can be rewarding, especially for people with a strong idea and few responsibilities. However, for the majority, gaining experience first offers a safer and more effective path to successful entrepreneurship.

drills: Sửa lỗi: Despite working from home is convenient, it can be lonely.
Although working from home is convenient, it can be lonely.
Despite không đi với mệnh đề; dùng although.
Sửa lỗi: There are many advantages. For example save time.
There are many advantages. For example, people save commuting time.
Sau For example cần dấu phẩy và một câu đầy đủ.
Viết lại học thuật hơn: Working from home is very good.
Working from home offers considerable benefits for many employees.
Tránh tính từ chung chung (very good).
Sửa lỗi: In the other hand, people feel isolated.
On the other hand, people may feel isolated.
Cụm đúng là On the other hand; thêm may để thận trọng.
Sửa lỗi: Companies can reduce cost of office.
Companies can reduce the cost of office space.
Thiếu mạo từ the và danh từ đầy đủ (office space).
Sửa lỗi: I think that remote working will became more popular.
I think that remote working will become more popular.
Sau will dùng động từ nguyên mẫu: become.

speaking.title: Work, jobs and business
speaking.instruction_vi: Part 2 mô tả một công việc/doanh nghiệp; Part 3 nêu giả định và dự đoán về tương lai nghề nghiệp.
speaking.focus: Dùng will/going to để nói kế hoạch và dự đoán; nối ý trái ngược bằng although/however khi trả lời Part 3.
part1: Do you work or are you a student?
What kind of job would you like to do in the future?
Have you ever had a part-time job?
Would you prefer to work for a large company or a small one?
speaking.part2: Describe a successful small business that you know. You should say what the business is, where it is, how you know about it, and explain why you think it is successful.
part3: Why do many young people want to start their own business?
How will technology change the way people work in the future?
speaking.model_answer: I’d like to talk about a small bakery near my home that’s run by a couple in their forties. It’s on a quiet street, not in a shopping centre, so I was surprised the first time I saw a long queue outside it early in the morning. I started going there about three years ago because a friend recommended their bread, and now I go almost every weekend. I think there are several reasons why it’s so successful. First, the quality is consistently good – they bake everything fresh, and when something is sold out, it’s sold out. Second, they really know their customers. The owners remember people’s names and what they usually buy, and they often give a small extra cake to children. And third, they’ve adapted over time. At the beginning they only sold bread, but they noticed many office workers passing by, so they started selling sandwiches and coffee at lunchtime. To me, it shows that a business doesn’t have to be big to be successful; it just has to understand the people it serves.
extensions: Why do many young people want to start their own business?
Nêu 2 lý do (tự do, kiếm nhiều tiền/đam mê) → ví dụ trên mạng xã hội → thừa nhận rủi ro: “However, most start-ups fail…”.
Liệt kê 2–3 phẩm chất (lắng nghe, công bằng, ghi nhận) → ví dụ cụ thể → kết: nhân viên nghỉ việc vì người quản lý.
How will technology change the way people work in the future?
Dự đoán bằng will → ví dụ AI, làm việc từ xa → nghề mới xuất hiện → kết: cần học suốt đời.
Is job security more important than a high salary?
Phụ thuộc giai đoạn cuộc đời → người trẻ vs người có gia đình → kết luận cá nhân có lý do.
